title: Floating Ferrofluid
description: Blobs of magnetic fluid floating in front of a loudspeaker that drives them in real time. The cone pumps with the bass and the sound modulates the fluid — bass swells the whole body and throws the Rosensweig spikes taller, treble bristles them finer, and each thump shoves the blobs outward before they settle back. Turn on the mic to feed it live sound; with no mic it runs on a synthetic kick so it's never still. It's rendered per pixel from a metaball field in a WebGL shader — the surface normal from the field gradient, shaded like oily black chrome with diffuse, a tight specular, a procedural environment reflection and Fresnel sheen — over the coned driver, its dust cap and rubber surround. Move the mouse to lean the spikes like a magnet; blobs, size, field, spikes, speaker drive, drift, viscosity and hue are live.
